objective: Students will describe the levels of structural organization of the human body and explain how homeostasis is maintained through negative feedback.
hook: Your body is doing about 100 things right now to keep you exactly the same — how?
bellRinger: List every 'level' you can think of between a single atom and a whole human. (60 seconds.)
agenda: Bell ringer (5) · Go over (5) · Launch: organization & homeostasis (12) · Video (6) · Guided notes (9) · Recap sheet (8) · Exit ticket (3)
assessment: Exit ticket: put the 6 levels of organization in order and name the 4 parts of a feedback loop.

questions: What are the four parts of a feedback loop, in order?
Is sweating an example of negative or positive feedback? Why?
Which level of organization is a group of the SAME cells working together?

videoPlacement: After the launch, before guided notes — the Amoeba Sisters clip nails the feedback loop.

script.title: Bell ringer
script.do: Post the atom-to-human listing task; let them struggle a moment.
options: Have a few read their lists aloud
script.say: How many steps did you find between an atom and you?

script.title: Go over
script.do: Build the 6 levels on the board from their lists.
options: Cold-call for an example of each level
script.say: Small to big: which is a group of the same cells?

script.title: Launch — organization & homeostasis
script.do: Run the deck: anatomy vs physiology, the 6 levels, homeostasis, the negative-feedback loop.
options: Act out the feedback loop: student = thermostat
script.say: Your body has a set point — what happens when you drift off it?

script.title: Video
script.do: Play the short Amoeba Sisters clip; students answer the 3 video questions.
options: Pause after the feedback loop and have them name the 4 parts
script.say: Catch the four parts as they go by.

script.title: Guided notes
script.do: Fill the notes together: word bank, the two concept sections + diagrams, then Check-Your-Understanding solo.
script.say: These exact terms are what the quiz asks.

script.title: Recap sheet
script.do: Start the recap worksheet: label the pyramid, match term to function, short explains.
options: Assign the CK-12 lesson as the graded recap instead if short on time
script.say: Label first, then explain in your own words.

script.title: Exit ticket
script.do: Collect the levels-order + feedback-parts exit ticket at the door.
script.say: Order the levels, name the loop.

notes:
## Body Organization & Homeostasis
**Anatomy** = the study of structure (what a part is). **Physiology** = the study of function (what it does).
**Levels of organization:** chemical → cell → tissue → organ → organ system → organism.
**Homeostasis** = keeping the internal environment stable. Most control is by **negative feedback**: a stimulus pushes a variable off its set point; a receptor detects it; the control center compares it to the set point; an effector produces a response that reverses the change.

examples.label: Concept 1 — the six levels of organization
examples.prompt: How does the body build from atoms up to a whole person?
steps: Atoms join into molecules — the {{chemical|2.4cm}} level.
Molecules build a {{cell|1.8cm}}, the smallest unit of life.
Many similar cells form a {{tissue|2cm}}; several tissues form an {{organ|2cm}}.
Organs that share a job form an {{organ system|2.6cm}}; all systems together make the {{organism|2.4cm}}.
examples.answer: chemical → cell → tissue → organ → organ system → organism

examples.label: Concept 2 — homeostasis by negative feedback
examples.prompt: You get too hot. How does your body pull you back to normal?

examples.figureCaption: Negative feedback: the response reverses the original change
steps: A change pushes a variable off its set point — the {{stimulus|2.2cm}}.
A {{receptor|2.2cm}} detects the change and sends the signal in.
The {{control center|2.6cm}} (often the brain) compares it to the set point.
An {{effector|2.2cm}} makes a response that {{reverses|2.2cm}} the change — bringing you back to normal.
examples.answer: stimulus → receptor → control center → effector → response (reverses the change)

youTry.prompt: Put in order, smallest to largest: organ, cell, organism, tissue, organ system, chemical.
youTry.answer: chemical, cell, tissue, organ, organ system, organism

youTry.prompt: Shivering when you get cold — negative or positive feedback? Explain in one sentence.
youTry.answer: Negative feedback — shivering makes heat to REVERSE the drop in temperature, back toward the set point.

youTry.prompt: Why is the heart an organ and not a tissue?
youTry.answer: It is made of two or more different tissues working together, which defines an organ.

vocab.definition: a control loop whose response reverses the change

slides.heading: You are holding steady right now
bullets: Your temperature, blood sugar, and water are all being held near a **set point** — automatically.
Anatomy asks *what* you're made of; physiology asks *how* it works.
Today: the 6 levels you're built from, and the loop that keeps you stable.

slides.heading: Two words that split the whole course
bullets: Every unit this year is one of those two questions about a body system.

vocab.definition: a group of similar cells with one job
two or more tissues working together

slides.heading: Six levels, small to large
bullets: Each level is built from the one below it.
A tissue = same cells; an organ = different tissues together.

slides.heading: Homeostasis = holding the set point
bullets: The body keeps conditions (temp, water, glucose) near a **set point**.
Drift off it, and a **negative feedback** loop pulls you back.
Four parts: **stimulus → receptor → control center → effector**.

slides.heading: Negative doesn't mean bad
slides.mistake: 'Negative feedback' means the response goes in the OPPOSITE direction of the change — it REVERSES it. Sweating when hot is negative feedback, and it's good for you.
slides.note: Negative = reverses. Positive = amplifies (rarer, e.g. childbirth).

problems: Why is the stomach an organ and not a tissue?

A runner's body temperature climbs during a race, then their sweat glands kick in and it drops back. Name each part of this feedback loop (stimulus, receptor, control center, effector) and say why it is NEGATIVE feedback.

procedure: Order the levels smallest to largest.
Match each term to what it does.
For feedback: find the stimulus, receptor, control center, and effector, then check the response REVERSES the change.

exitTicket: Put the 6 levels of organization in order (smallest to largest).
Name the 4 parts of a negative feedback loop, in order.

answers: The stomach is made of several different tissues (muscle, lining/epithelium, nerve) working together, and 'organ' means two or more tissues combined.

Stimulus = body temp rises; receptor = skin/hypothalamus senses it; control center = hypothalamus (brain) compares to the set point; effector = sweat glands produce sweat. It is NEGATIVE feedback because the response (cooling) reverses the original change (heating).
